## Page 3002

So, by Allah, nothing has shown them the immensity of what He has described of Himself, and of what His grasp encompasses, except their awareness of how small its counterpart in themselves is. This is what has been instilled in their minds, and He created their hearts with knowledge of it. Whatever Allah has described of Himself and named through His Messenger, we name as He has named it, without presuming to know anything beyond it. We do neither of these two things: we neither deny what He has described nor presume to know what He has not described.” End of quotation.

That being so, if created things are assumed to be like a ball, and this is how He grasps them and casts them, then what He has explained to us of His greatness is simply how created things stand in relation to Him, in terms whose counterpart we can understand from ourselves. Moreover, what is in the Quran and hadith makes clear that, if He wills, He grasps them and does with them what has been mentioned, as He will do on the Day of Resurrection; and if He wills, He does not do so. He is therefore able to grasp them and cast them like a ball. The encompassing of them that this entails is evident. If He wills, however, He does not do so. In every case, He is distinct from them, not co-located with them.

It is well known that any one of us—and to Allah belongs the highest example—who has a mustard seed may, if he wishes, grasp it so that his grasp encompasses it. If he wishes, he may leave it ungrasped and instead place it beneath him. In both cases, he is distinct from it. Likewise, whether the Throne is assumed to encompass created things—as a sphere encompasses what is within it—or is said to be above them without encompassing them, like the surface of the earth on which we stand in relation to its interior, or a dome in relation to what lies beneath it, or otherwise:

On either assumption, the Throne is above created things, and the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is above it. When the servant turns towards Allah, he directs himself upwards, not downwards. This discussion is completed by explaining:

---

## Page 3003

the third point:

We say: either the Throne is spherical like the celestial spheres and encompasses them, or it is above them without being spherical. If the former is the case, it is well known—and agreed upon by those knowledgeable in this matter—that the celestial spheres are round and spherical in shape; that the upward direction is towards the outer surface, which is convex; and that the downward direction is towards the centre. The celestial spheres have only two directions: up and down.

The six directions, however, pertain to a living creature, which has six sides. It faces one direction, which is therefore in front of it, and leaves another behind, which is therefore behind it. One direction is to its right, another to its left, another towards its head, and another towards its feet. These six directions have no fixed character in themselves; rather, they depend on relative position and relation. Thus, what is to the right of one creature may be to the left of another; what is in front of one may be behind another; and what is above one may be below another.

The upward and downward directions of the celestial spheres, however, do not change: the outer surface is above, and the centre is below. This is so even though the face of the earth, which Allah has laid out for His creatures and made firm with mountains, is where people, beasts, trees, plants, mountains, and flowing rivers are found. As for the other side of the earth, the sea surrounds it, and there are no human beings there, nor anything associated with them. Were anyone assumed to be there, they would be on the surface of the earth and would not be

---

## Page 3004

the case that those on this side were beneath those on the other, or that those on the other side were beneath them. Likewise, the celestial spheres encompass the centre, yet neither side of a sphere is beneath the other, nor is the northern pole beneath the southern pole, or vice versa. The northern pole is, however, the one visible to us above the earth, and its altitude depends on people’s distance from the equator. For someone thirty degrees from the equator, for example, the pole’s altitude is thirty degrees. This is what is called the latitude of a locality.

Just as the sides all around the earth and the rounded sides of the celestial sphere are not above or below one another, so too the living creatures, plants, and heavy objects upon the earth cannot be said to be beneath those on the other side. This is merely something a person imagines, involving a relative sense of “below.” Consider an ant walking beneath a ceiling: the ceiling is above it even though its feet face the ceiling. Likewise, someone suspended upside down remains beneath the sky even though their feet point towards it. Similarly, a person on one side of the earth or the celestial sphere imagines that the other side is beneath them. No two people who hold that the celestial spheres are spherical disagree on this matter.

The spherical form of the celestial spheres is not only the position of astronomers and mathematicians; it is also the position of Muslim scholars. Abū al-Hasan ibn al-Munādī, Abū Muhammad ibn Hazm, Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī, and others have stated that Muslim scholars agree on this. And He has said

---

## Page 3005

, exalted is He:

“And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each floating in an orbit.”

Ibn ‘Abbās said: “A whorl, like the whorl of a spindle.” In Arabic, *falak* means something round. Hence the expression *tafallaka thady al-jāriya*: “The young woman’s breast has become rounded.” Everyone who knows that the celestial spheres are round knows that the encompassing sphere is above its centre on every side. In their view, anyone who imagines that someone on one side of a celestial sphere actually has someone on its opposite side beneath him is mistaken.

Since this is so, if the Throne is assumed to be round and to encompass created things, it would be the highest of them and their roof—above them without qualification. A person could therefore turn towards it and towards what is above it only upwards, never in any other direction. Anyone who turned towards the ninth sphere, the eighth, or any other celestial sphere in a direction other than upwards would be ignorant, by the agreement of all rational people. How much more so when turning towards the Throne or towards what is above it! The most that can be supposed is that it is spherical. Allah Most High encompasses all created things in a manner befitting His majesty, for the seven heavens and the earth in His hand are smaller than a chickpea in the hand of one of us.

As for the statement: “If it is spherical, and Allah is beyond it, encompassing it and distinct from it, what is the point of a servant turning towards Allah when supplicating and worshipping Him, directing himself upwards rather than downwards? There would then be no difference, when supplicating, between turning upwards and towards the other directions that surround

---

## Page 3006

the supplicant. Yet we find in our hearts an impulse that seeks what is above, turning neither right nor left. Explain to us, then, this compelling impulse that we find in our hearts and with which we were naturally endowed.”

The reply is:

This question arises only from the mistaken supposition that half the celestial sphere lies beneath the earth and beneath the human beings and animals on its surface. This is a grave error. If the celestial sphere were beneath the earth on one side, it would be beneath it on every side. It would necessarily follow that the celestial sphere was beneath the earth without qualification. This reverses the facts, for the celestial sphere is above the earth without qualification.

The “astronomers” say: If a hole were bored through the earth in the direction of our feet, and a heavy object—such as a stone or the like—were dropped into it, it would come to rest at the centre. Even if another stone were dropped from that side, the two would meet at the centre. If two people, rather than two stones, were imagined meeting at the centre, their feet would meet, and neither would be beneath the other. Rather, both would be above the centre, and both would be beneath the celestial sphere.

The same applies to east and west. If one man were in the east, whether in the sky or on earth, and another in the west, whether in the sky or on earth, neither would be beneath the other. This would be so whether his head, feet, belly, back, or side faced the sky or the earth. If either sought what is above the celestial sphere, he would seek it only upwards, not in the direction of his feet, his right, or his left, for two reasons:

(First, what he seeks is nearer to him in the upward direction than in any other direction. If a man or an angel were imagined ascending to heaven or to what is above it, then his ascent in the direction of his head would be

---

## Page 3007

nearer, if that were possible for him. No rational person would say that he should bore through the earth and then ascend from the other side, or that he should go right, left, forwards, or backwards to some other place on earth and then ascend. Wherever he went would be equivalent to his present position or below it, and the celestial sphere would still be above him. Travelling in any of these five directions would therefore entail a longer journey and needless exertion.

If a man wished to address the sun or the moon, he would address it only upwards, even though the sun and moon rise and set, moving away from the point directly overhead. How much more, then, does this apply to Him who is always above everything, who neither sets nor disappears—glorified and exalted is He?

Just as motion, such as that of a stone, tends towards its centre by the shortest route—a straight line—how could the deliberate seeking that arises in the hearts of Allah’s servants turn away from the short, straight path to a long, winding route? Allah Most High created His servants with a sound and upright innate disposition, except for those whom the devils have led astray, taking them away from the innate disposition with which they were created.

(Second:

If a person directs his aim downwards, without any upward orientation, his aim will terminate at the centre. If he seeks Him in front of him, behind him, to his right, or to his left, without aiming upwards, his aim will terminate somewhere in the air. He must therefore necessarily aim upwards, whether or not he also aims in these other directions.

Suppose he were to say, “I seek Him to the right while also aiming upwards, or from below while also aiming upwards.” This would be like someone saying, “I wish to perform Hajj from the Maghrib, so I shall go to Khurāsān and then go to Mecca.” Indeed, it would be like someone saying, “I shall ascend to the celestial spheres, so I shall descend into the earth and then

---

## Page 3008

ascend to the celestial sphere from the other side.” Although this is possible in terms of what can be done, it is impossible in the sense that a person seeking his goal cannot will such a course. It runs contrary to the innate disposition, for a person seeks his goal by the shortest route, especially when the One he seeks is the One he worships and relies upon. If he turns towards Him by a path other than the straight path, his journey is inverted and reversed.

Moreover, in his journey and intention, such a person combines negation with affirmation: drawing nearer to the One he seeks while moving farther away from Him, seeking Him while recoiling from Him. For if he turns towards Him by the most distant and remote route, abandoning the nearest and shortest one, he combines two contradictory intentions. His intention to seek Him is therefore not complete, since a complete intention excludes its contradiction and opposite. This is known through the innate disposition.

If someone loves the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with complete love and seeks him—or loves anyone else, whether that love is praiseworthy or blameworthy—then whenever his love is complete and he seeks his beloved, he takes the shortest route by which he can reach him.

This differs from the case in which his love is conflicted. For example, he may love something that religion disapproves of loving, so that his desire continues to urge him to seek it while his reason forbids him from doing so. You therefore see him approaching it by a roundabout route, as people commonly say: “One foot forward and one foot back.”

Likewise, if his religious commitment is deficient, and his reason bids him go to the mosque, undertake jihad, or pursue other goals that religion commends but the soul dislikes, he continues towards that goal by a roundabout route, moving slowly along the way. All this is known through the innate disposition.

---

## Page 3009

Similarly, if someone does not intend to go in person, but wishes instead to address the one he seeks, call upon him, or the like, then, if his intention is complete, he addresses him from the nearest direction from which his call can be heard and his aim achieved. If a man were in a high place and another wished to call to him, the latter would turn towards him and call. If he lowered his head into a well and called in such a way that the other could hear his voice, this would be possible. Yet someone whose intention is to make himself heard would not naturally do this without some overriding benefit. Such conduct occurs only when the intention is weak or something similar.

As for the “hadith of lowering,” reported from Abū Hurayrah and Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with them both, al-Tirmidhī and others transmitted it through al-Hasan al-Basrī from Abū Hurayrah. Its chain is interrupted, since al-Hasan did not hear from Abū Hurayrah. However, it is strengthened by the report of Abū Dharr attributed to the Prophet. If it is authentic, its meaning agrees with this explanation, for his words:

“If one of you were lowered by a rope, he would descend upon Allah”

express only a hypothetical supposition: were such lowering to occur, what was lowered would come down upon Him. Yet no one can lower anything onto Allah, for He is high above in His essence. When something is lowered towards the earth, it stops at the centre and does not rise towards the other side. But if the lowering were hypothetically assumed, the stated consequence would follow.

The same applies to what the questioner mentioned: if it were supposed that a servant sought Him from that direction, He, glorified be He, would hear his words, and the servant would be turning towards Him with his heart. Yet the innate disposition prevents this, because a complete intention to seek something is incompatible with intending its opposite. Thus, just as the intrinsically upper direction is incompatible with

---

## Page 3010

the lower direction, so too seeking the One who is high in His essence is incompatible with seeking Him from below. Just as something descending into the earth cannot rise towards the other side—because that side is above, and its height repels the descending object, just as the upper direction on our side repels heavy objects rising towards it, so that a heavy object rises only when something lifts it, counteracting its inherent tendency to descend—so too, something descending from the earth’s upper surface to its lowest point, the centre, cannot rise from there towards the other side unless something lifts it, counteracting its inherent tendency to descend towards the centre. If the impelling force were assumed to be stronger, it would carry the object upwards towards the celestial sphere on that side and raise it towards Allah.

This is called a descent only in view of the notion in the minds of those being addressed that whatever moves in the direction of their feet is descending. It is called a descent, while the act of making it descend is called a lowering. Yet it is truly a lowering only as far as the centre; beyond that, it is merely an extension of the rope and bucket, not a lowering. Both the consequence and the condition, however, are hypothetical, not actual.

For he said:

“If one were to lower something, it would descend.”

That is, if a lowering were supposed, a descent would likewise be supposed. It would be a lowering and a descent if the heavens were supposed to be beneath the earth. This supposition is not true; its purpose, however, is to illustrate encompassment and highness on every side. This hypothetical act is impossible for us; we have no power to perform it. Thus, no such lowering can be conceived, nor can anything be conceived as descending upon Allah. Allah, however, has the power to pass a rope through from here to there. Yet, in His case, this would not constitute a lowering, and so it would not constitute a descent upon Him. It is as though He were to pass a rope through from pole to pole, or from the place of sunrise to the place of sunset

---

## Page 3011

and we supposed that the rope passed through the centre of the earth. Allah has power over all of this. On this supposition, it makes no difference in relation to Him whether He passes the rope through from our right to our left, from in front of us to behind us, or from above our heads to beneath our feet, when the rope passes through the earth. In every supposed case, He has passed the rope from one side of the encompassing sphere to the other, passing through the centre. On the supposition that His grasp encompasses the heavens and the earth, the rope with which He is supposed to have passed through the universe would reach Him. None of this, in relation to Him, is called a lowering or a descent.

In relation to us, however, what is beneath our feet is below us, and what is above our heads is above us. Whatever we lower from the direction of our heads towards our feet, we imagine to be descending. Thus, if one of us were supposed to lower a rope, it would descend upon whatever was there. Yet this is a supposition that is impossible for us to realize. Its purpose is to illustrate the encompassing nature of the Creator—glorified and exalted be He—just as He has explained that He grasps the heavens and folds up the earth, and other such matters that illustrate His encompassment of created things. This is why, at the conclusion of this hadith, he recited:

“He is the First and the Last, the Most High and the Most Near, and He has knowledge of all things.”

All of this, however, assumes that the hadith is authentic. For when al-Tirmidhī narrated it, he said:

“Some hadith scholars interpreted it as meaning that it descended upon Allah’s knowledge.”

Some proponents of divine indwelling and union imagine that this hadith supports their false doctrine: that He dwells in His essence in every place, that His existence is the very existence of places, and similar claims.

The correct conclusion is that the hadith, if authentic, indicates none of this. For his statement:

---

## Page 3012

“If someone were to lower a rope, it would descend”

indicates that He is not within the person lowering it, nor within the rope, the bucket, or anything else, and implies that He is in that direction. Likewise, interpreting it as referring to His knowledge is a manifestly unsound interpretation, akin to the interpretations of the Jahmiyyah. Rather, assuming its authenticity, it would indicate His encompassment. It is known that Allah has power to encompass all things, and it is known from the Quran and Sunnah that this will occur on the Day of Resurrection. Affirming this in general contradicts neither reason nor revelation. However, we speak only of what we know, and refrain from speaking of what we do not know. If someone doubts a premise upon which a proof rests, he ought to remain uncertain about its conclusion until the truth becomes clear to him; otherwise, let him remain silent about what he does not know.

Once this is clear, the same applies to someone seeking Him: he seeks Him in that direction. If we were hypothetically to do so, we would, on this supposition, be seeking Him. Yet seeking Him by directing ourselves that way is impossible for us, because a complete, resolute intention necessarily entails pursuing what is intended as far as one is able.

For this reason, elsewhere—when discussing the disagreement over whether a person is punished for an intention unaccompanied by action—we explained that a “resolute intention” necessarily entails doing whatever one can to accomplish what one intends. Whenever a person fails to do what is within his power, his intention is not resolute; rather, it is an inclination. Whoever inclines towards an evil deed but does not commit it has no sin recorded against him. If he abandons it for Allah’s sake, a good deed is recorded for him. This is why there is a distinction between Joseph’s inclination—peace be upon him—and that of the minister’s wife, as stated by

---

## Page 3013

Imam Ahmad: “Inclination is of two kinds: passing thoughts and persistent resolve.” Joseph—peace be upon him—experienced an inclination which he abandoned for Allah’s sake, and he was rewarded for doing so. Her inclination, however, was a persistent resolve: she did whatever she could to attain her desire, even though she did not achieve her aim.

Those who hold that a person is punished for an intention cited the Prophet’s words—may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“When two Muslims confront one another with their swords, both the killer and the one killed are in the Fire.” They asked, “O Messenger of Allah, we understand about the killer, but what of the one killed?” He replied, “He intended to kill his fellow.”

Another version reads:

“He was eager to kill his fellow.”

This man had a resolute intention and did whatever he could, even though he did not achieve his aim. His case is therefore like that of the minister’s wife. Whenever an intention is resolute, the person necessarily does whatever he can to achieve his aim. If he can attain it by a direct route, then, with a complete intention, he cannot seek to attain it by a distant route in the opposite direction.

For this reason, when Allah’s servants are in distress, supplicate to Him, and direct their intention fully toward Him, they can only turn directly toward Him. They therefore turn upward, rather than in any other direction, because that is the straight, near path; every other route entails distance, deviation, and length. With the complete intention characteristic of the supplicant, the worshipper, and the petitioner in desperate need, a person cannot turn toward Him except upward. He cannot turn toward Him in any other direction, just as he cannot lower a rope that would descend to Him. The two cases are thus alike, and Allah knows best.

As for revelation, the messengers—may Allah’s blessings be upon them—were sent to perfect and affirm the innate disposition, not to replace or alter it. The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said in the hadith recorded by both al-Bukhārī and Muslim:

---

## Page 3014

“Every child is born upon the innate disposition; then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to an intact offspring. Do you see any mutilation in it?”

Allah Most High says:

“So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, in accordance with the innate disposition with which Allah created mankind. There is no changing Allah’s creation. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.”

Thus, in worship and supplication, the revealed law accords with the innate disposition, unlike the ways of those astray among the polytheists, the philosophizing Sabians, and others. They have altered the innate disposition in both knowledge and will, contradicting both reason and revelation, as we have explained at length elsewhere.

It is established through several routes in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“When any of you stands to pray, he must not spit in front of him, for Allah is before him; nor to his right, for there is an angel to his right. Rather, he should spit to his left or beneath his foot.”

Another version states that “he permitted spitting into one’s garment.”

In the well-known hadith that Abū Razīn narrated from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—he related:

“When the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—announced that everyone would be alone with his Lord, Abū Razīn asked him, ‘How can He accommodate us, O Messenger of Allah, when He is One and we are so many?’ He replied, ‘I shall tell you of something comparable among Allah’s wonders: this moon is one of Allah’s signs. Each of you sees it while alone with it. Allah is greater still.’”

It is well known that someone who turns toward the moon and addresses it—assuming that he could address it—does not

---

## Page 3015

turn toward it except by facing it, even though it is above him. Thus, he faces it while it is above him. It is contrary to the innate disposition for him to turn his back on it and address it while fully intent on addressing it, even though doing so is possible. Only someone whose purpose is not to address it directly would do that—as when someone does not intend to address a particular person directly, so he turns his face away and addresses someone else, intending the first person to hear his words. When there is no impediment, however, he turns directly toward him. Likewise, when the servant stands to pray, he faces his Lord, who is above him. He calls upon Him as being before him, not to his right or left, and as being above him, not below him, just as in the hypothetical case of addressing the moon.

It is established in the two Sahīh collections that he said:

“Some people must stop raising their eyes during prayer, or their sight will not return to them.”

The scholars agree that worshippers are forbidden to raise their eyes toward the sky. Ahmad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sīrīn:

“The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—used to raise his eyes toward the sky during prayer, until Allah Most High revealed: ‘Successful indeed are the believers, those who are humble in their prayers.’ Thereafter, his gaze did not extend beyond the place of his prostration.”

This is among the prescriptions of the revealed law that perfect the innate disposition. For someone who supplicates and petitions, and who is commanded to observe humility—which means humble submission and silence—it is not fitting to look toward the One whom he invokes and petitions. Rather, it befits him to bow his head and lower his gaze before him.

The prohibition against worshippers raising their eyes during prayer is not a refutation of “those who affirm the divine attributes,” who say that He is above the Throne, as some ignorant Jahmiyyah suppose. For the Jahmiyyah make no distinction

---

## Page 3016

between the Throne and the depths of the sea: all are alike. If that were so, one would not be forbidden to look in one direction and commanded to turn one’s gaze toward another, since both directions are alike according to the Jahmiyyah.

Moreover, if that were so, the prohibition against raising one’s gaze would apply in every circumstance. Yet Allah Most High says:

“We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward heaven.”

Thus, the servant is not forbidden to raise his gaze altogether; rather, he is forbidden to do so when he is commanded to observe humility, for lowering one’s gaze perfects humility. As Allah Most High says:

“With their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves.”

And Allah Most High says:

“You will see them exposed to it, humbled by disgrace, looking with a furtive glance.”

Furthermore, if looking up toward the sky were forbidden while there were no God in heaven, there would be no difference between raising one’s gaze toward the sky and turning it in any other direction. Had his purpose been to forbid people to believe that Allah is in heaven, or to direct their hearts upward, he would have explained that to them, just as he explained all the other rulings. How could that be, when neither Allah’s Book, nor His Messenger’s Sunnah, nor the statements of the early generations of the Muslim community contain a single word saying that Allah is not above the Throne, that He is not above heaven, that He is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither co-located with it nor separate from it, or that the servant should not direct himself upward rather than in other directions when calling upon Him?

Indeed, for all the negations the Jahmiyyah assert—and claim to be the truth—they have not a single word of support from Allah’s Book, His Messenger’s Sunnah, or the statements of any of the community’s early generations and imams. Rather, the Book, the Sunnah, and the statements of the early generations and imams are filled with evidence indicating the opposite of their position. Yet they say:

---

## Page 3017

“The apparent meaning of that is disbelief, so we reinterpret it or entrust it to Allah.” Thus, according to their position, the Book, the Sunnah, and the statements of the early generations and the imams contain nothing on this subject whose apparent meaning is not disbelief, and nothing on this subject that expresses faith. Yet the negation they claim to be the truth—which, according to them, every believer, or the select among the believers, must believe—was never uttered by any messenger, prophet, or heir to the prophets and messengers. What the prophets and their heirs did utter is not, according to them, the truth; rather, its apparent meaning contradicts the truth. Indeed, their most adept thinkers know that it contradicts the truth both outwardly and inwardly. Some of them, however, claim that the prophets could only address people in terms contrary to the inward truth, and therefore resorted to deception and falsehood for the benefit of the common people.

They should be asked: Why, then, did the prophets not disclose this inward truth to their intelligent and virtuous close followers, if what these people claim is true? It is well known that the messengers’ close followers likewise upheld affirmation, and that none of them ever expressed negation—unless someone falsely attributes it to one of them. One example is the statement attributed to ʿUmar:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abū Bakr would converse, while I was like a man of the Zanj between them.”

The scholars agree that this is fabricated. The same applies to what is related about ʿAlī and his household: that they possessed inward knowledge contrary to the outward knowledge held by the majority of the Muslim community. It is established in the authentic hadith collections and elsewhere, on the authority of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that they possessed no secret from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that other people did not possess, nor any written document apart from what was on the sheet, which contained:

“Blood-money payments, the ransoming of captives, and the rule that a Muslim is not to be killed in retaliation for a disbeliever.”

---

## Page 3018

Furthermore, it is well known that if someone whom Allah has appointed as a guide and a conveyor of His message in clear Arabic never says anything except what contradicts the actual inward truth, then he is closer to misguidance and deception than to guidance and clear explanation. A detailed refutation of them belongs elsewhere.

The point is that everything conveyed by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on this subject and others is true, each part confirming the rest. It accords with the innate disposition of created beings and the clear reason and sound intentions with which they have been endowed. It contradicts neither clear reason, sound intent, upright innate disposition, nor authentic reports firmly established from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Only someone who accepts false reports, understands them to mean what they do not indicate, or holds something to be rational knowledge when it is actually ignorance, or spiritual unveiling when it is actually obscuration, supposes these to conflict—if what he holds contradicts an authentic report. Otherwise, he is using clear reason or genuine spiritual unveiling to challenge something he supposes to have been transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when it is actually falsely attributed to him, or wording he supposes to signify something when it does not.

An example is their discussion of the saying attributed to him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The Black Stone is Allah’s right hand on earth. Whoever clasps it and kisses it, it is as though he has shaken hands with Allah and kissed His right hand.”

They supposed that this and similar statements require figurative interpretation. This is a mistake on their part—even supposing that this wording were established from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. For this wording explicitly indicates that the Stone is not one of Allah’s attributes, since he said:

“It is Allah’s right hand on earth.”

Thus, the qualification “on earth” indicates that it is not His hand in

---

## Page 3019

an absolute sense, and thus it is not His actual hand. His saying,

“Whoever clasps it and kisses it, it is as though he has shaken hands with Allah and kissed His right hand,”

explicitly indicates that whoever clasps and kisses it is neither shaking hands with Allah nor kissing His right hand. For the thing compared is not the thing to which it is compared. He used the expression “it is as though,” which explicitly conveys a comparison. Since the wording explicitly indicates that it has been accorded the position of the right hand, not that it is the right hand itself, anyone who believes that its apparent meaning is that it is the actual right hand is uttering a manifest falsehood.

All of this is on the supposition that the Throne is spherical, whether it is the ninth celestial sphere or something other than the ninth celestial sphere. It has become clear that its surface is the roof over created things, that it is above them on every side, and that nothing in the heavens or the earth can be above it. On this supposition, anyone directing himself toward what is above the Throne directs himself only upward. Neither innate disposition nor revealed law allows him, when fully intent on this, to turn toward any other of the six directions. Rather, he also faces Him, although He is above him, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, illustrated through the example of the moon—and to Allah belongs the highest description. He explained that if such a thing is possible in the case of the moon, which is one of Allah Most High’s signs, then the Creator is more exalted and greater.

If, on the other hand, the Throne is supposed not to be spherical, but to be above the world on the side corresponding to the earth’s surface, and above the spherical celestial spheres—just as the earth’s surface, laid out for mankind, is above half of the spherical earth—or if any other configuration is supposed in which the Throne is above everything else without being spherical, then under every such supposition we turn toward Allah only upward, not toward any other direction.

---

## Page 3020

It has thus become clear that, under every supposition, one may direct oneself toward Allah only upward, while He is upon His Throne, distinct from His creation. Whether it is further supposed that He encompasses created things—as He encompasses them when they are in His grasp—or that He is above them without grasping and encompassing them, He is, on either supposition, above them and distinct from them. It is therefore clear that, on this supposition concerning the Creator and this supposition concerning the Throne, no objectionable consequence or contradiction follows. This dispels every doubt. Such doubts arise only from two false beliefs.

The first is to suppose that, if the Throne is spherical and Allah is above it, Allah must necessarily be spherical; then to believe that, if He is spherical, one may direct oneself toward something spherical—such as the ninth celestial sphere—from every direction. Both beliefs are erroneous and misguided. Although Allah is above the Throne, and even on the view that the Throne is spherical—whether it is the ninth celestial sphere or something else—it is impermissible to suppose that He resembles the celestial spheres in their shapes, just as it is impermissible to suppose that He resembles them in their dimensions or attributes. Glory be to Him! Exalted is He far above what the wrongdoers say!

Rather, it has become clear that He is far too great and mighty for created things, in relation to Him, to be like the contents of a celestial sphere in relation to that sphere. In relation to Him, they are smaller than a chickpea, a peppercorn, or the like in the hand of one of us. If a chickpea or a peppercorn—or even a dirham, a dinar, a ball that children play with, or something similar—is in a person’s hand, beneath him, or in some comparable position, would any rational person, recognizing that the person is above it and encompasses it, imagine that the person must be like a celestial sphere? Allah—and to Allah belongs the highest description—is far too great for such a thing to be supposed of Him. This is imagined of Him only by

---

## Page 3021

those who

“have not given Allah His due. On the Day of Resurrection, the entire earth will be in His grasp, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glory be to Him! Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him!”

Likewise, their “second belief”—that one may direct oneself toward a celestial sphere from any of the six directions—is erroneous by the agreement of rational people versed in astronomy, as well as rational people who know that a firm intention necessarily leads to carrying out what is intended insofar as possible.

It has thus become clear that each of the two premises is erroneous according to both reason and revelation, and that hearts may direct themselves toward Him only upward, not in any other direction, under every conceivable supposition: whether the Throne is the ninth celestial sphere or something else; whether it encompasses the celestial sphere and is spherical in shape, or is above it without being spherical; and whether the Creator—glory be to Him—encompasses created things as He encompasses them in His grasp, or is above them in the upward direction from us, above our heads, rather than in the opposite direction.

Under whichever supposition is proposed, both premises of the question are false. When we supplicate to Allah Most High, we direct ourselves toward Him only upward, not in any other direction, just as we have been innately disposed to do. The answer to the question thus becomes clear in several ways. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 3022

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

Do the Throne and the Kursī (Seat) actually exist, or are they metaphorical? Is it the position of Ahl al-Sunnah that Allah Most High spoke to Moses directly, from Himself to him, without an intermediary? And was what Moses saw light or fire?

He—may Allah be pleased with him—replied:

Praise be to Allah. The Throne does indeed exist, as established by the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations of this nation and its leading scholars. Likewise, the Kursī is established by the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the majority of the early generations.

It has been transmitted from some of them that “His Kursī” means His knowledge. This is a weak opinion, for Allah’s knowledge encompasses everything, as He says:

“Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge.”

Allah knows Himself, and He knows what has existed and what has not existed. Thus, interpreting the words as “His knowledge encompasses the heavens and the earth” would not be fitting here, particularly since He Most High says:

“Preserving them does not weary Him.”

That is, it neither burdens nor troubles Him. This is appropriate to power, not knowledge, and the transmitted reports bear this out. Nevertheless, the verses and hadiths concerning the Throne are more numerous still; they are explicit and transmitted through numerous independent chains.

---

## Page 3023

Some have also said that the Kursī is the Throne, but the majority hold that they are two distinct things.

As for Moses, all Muslims—both Ahl al-Sunnah and the adherents of religious innovation—agree that Allah spoke to him without an intermediary. No Muslim has said that there was an intermediary between Moses and Allah when He spoke to him: neither Ahl al-Sunnah, nor the Jahmiyyah, nor the Muʿtazilah, nor the Kullābiyyah, nor anyone else. They do, however, disagree over other aspects of this matter.

What Moses saw was fire, as the Quran explicitly states. It was also light, as stated in the hadith; and fire is light. Allah knows best.

---

## Page 3024

He was asked:

Two men disagreed about “the form of heaven and earth”: are they “two spherical bodies”? One said that they are spherical, while the other rejected this view, saying that it has no basis. What is correct?

He answered:

According to Muslim scholars, the heavens are spherical. More than one of the leading scholars of Islam has reported a Muslim consensus on this, including Abū al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Ja‘far ibn al-Munādī, one of the most eminent figures of the second generation of Imam Ahmad’s followers, who authored some four hundred works. Imam Abū Muhammad ibn Hazm and Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī also reported this consensus.

Scholars have transmitted this from the Companions and their successors through well-known chains of transmission. They have cited evidence for it from Allah’s Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, discussing it at length on the basis of scriptural evidence, although mathematical proofs have also been adduced.

I know of no recognized Muslim scholar who denied this, apart from a small group of dialecticians who, when they debated the astrologers and refuted the unsound aspects of their doctrine concerning conditions

---

## Page 3025

and influence, confused the issues by also debating mathematics with them. Speaking merely of what was possible, they said that the heavens might be square, hexagonal, or some other shape. They did not deny that they were spherical, but allowed the contrary as a possibility. I know of no one who categorically asserted that they are not spherical except ignorant people whose views carry no weight.

Among the proofs of this are the words of the Most High:

“It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each floating in an orbit.”

The Most High also says:

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each floats in an orbit.”

Ibn ‘Abbās and others among the early generations said:

“In a circle, like the whorl of a spindle.”

This explicitly indicates roundness and rotation. Its linguistic basis is that falak means something round. One says, tafallaka thadyu al-jāriyah, meaning that a girl’s breast has become rounded. The round whorl of a spindle is likewise called a falkah because of its roundness. Thus, scholars of Quranic exegesis and Arabic language agree that falak denotes something round. Knowledge of the meanings of Allah’s Book is derived through these two avenues: trustworthy authorities on Quranic exegesis among the early generations, and the language in which the Quran was revealed—Arabic.

The Most High says:

“He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night.”

They said that takwīr means winding something round. One says, kawwartu al-‘imāmah (“I wound the turban”) and kawwartuhā (“I wound it”), meaning that one wound it round. A round object is called a kārah, a form derived by changing its original wāw into an alif, since the wāw carried a vowel and was preceded by a fathah (a short a).

---

## Page 3026

It is also called a kurah (“sphere”), originally kūrah; the middle root letter has simply been omitted, as in thubah and qulah. Night and day, and all other aspects of time, follow motion, for time is the measure of motion, and motion inheres in the moving body. Thus, if time—which depends on motion, which in turn depends on the body—is described as circular, then the body has an even greater claim to roundness.

The Most High says:

“You will not see any inconsistency in the creation of the Most Merciful.”

The bodies in heaven are uniform, without difference or disparity—whereas triangular, quadrilateral, pentagonal, hexagonal and other such forms display disparities and differences in their angles and sides—since roundness pertains to the sides.

In the well-known hadith recorded in Sunan Abī Dāwūd and elsewhere, Jubayr ibn Mut‘im relates:

“A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, people are exhausted, wealth has perished, and families are hungry. Pray for rain for us, for we seek Allah’s intercession with you, and your intercession with Allah.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, glorified Allah until the effect of this could be seen on his Companions’ faces. He said, ‘Woe to you! Allah is not to be sought as an intercessor with any of His creation. Allah’s majesty is greater than that. His Throne is above His heavens like this’—and he gestured with his hand in the shape of a dome—‘and it creaks beneath Him as a new saddle creaks beneath its rider.’”

Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stated that the Throne is above the heavens like a dome. This indicates elevation and roundness.

---

## Page 3027

In the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:

“When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest and most central part of Paradise, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.”

A central position is possible only in something round. Iyās ibn Mu‘āwiyah said, “The sky is like a dome over the earth.” This fatwa cannot accommodate all the reports on this matter; I have merely written this in haste.

Sense perception, together with reason, also indicates this. It becomes apparent upon considering how the stars near the pole revolve in a narrow circuit around the north pole, while the stars in the middle of the sky revolve in a broad circuit, and observing their positions at the beginning and end of the night. Likewise, anyone who observes the sun at its rising, culmination, and setting—at all three times remaining at the same distance and having the same appearance to someone on the earth’s surface—will know that it travels in a circular orbit. Were its orbit square, then at its culmination it would be closer to the person directly beneath it than at sunrise and sunset. There are numerous proofs of this.

As for anyone who makes a claim contrary to the Book and the Sunnah, his claim is false, even if he maintains that he has evidence based on calculation. This is common among those who study “the celestial sphere and its phenomena.” An example is the claim of a group of ignorant people that the probable time of the crescent’s rising can be determined, so as to know when it will appear after its period of invisibility, by knowing its distance from the sun after separating from it at sunset, and by precisely determining the “arc of visibility,” which is a line laid out in a curve—a segment of a circle—

---

## Page 3028

at the time of the crescent’s first appearance. This claim is false. The eminent scholars of Islamic law have agreed that relying on this for determining the crescent is forbidden. Sensible practitioners of calculation likewise agree that the crescent’s visibility can never be determined with complete precision by calculation. For this reason, the masters of calculation did not undertake this; rather, they rejected it. Only some of their later practitioners discussed it in approximate terms. This is a departure from Allah’s religion and an alteration of it, resembling the Jews’ and Christians’ departure from what they were commanded concerning the crescent to the sun’s endpoint at the conjunction of the two discs—the period of the moon’s invisibility—rather than crescent-based months, and similar practices.

The postponement practised among the Arabs—which is an increase in disbelief, through which those who disbelieve go astray, permitting it one year and forbidding it another—is what the scholars of hadith, historical biography, Quranic commentary and other disciplines have described.

It is established in the two Sahīh collections, on the authority of Umar, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“We are an unlettered nation: we neither write nor calculate. Begin fasting when you sight it, and end fasting when you sight it.”

Whoever determines the crescent—which Allah has made a means of marking time for people and for Hajj—through writing and calculation is unsound in both reason and religion. Even when someone’s calculations are correct, the most he can do is determine the distance between the sun and the moon at sunset, for example. This is what is called the moon’s distance from the sun. But this does not establish that it will certainly be visible, or that it cannot possibly be seen.

---

## Page 3029

For “sighting” varies according to the elevation of the terrain, the clarity or murkiness of the atmosphere, the observer’s eyesight and its sharpness, how long or briefly one looks intently, whether one directs one’s gaze correctly, the number of people watching for the crescent, and the crescent’s thickness. It may not be visible at sunset, but afterwards its distance from the sun increases, so it grows brighter and emerges from the glare that prevents it from being seen; it then becomes visible.

Likewise, they have not agreed on a single angular measure for its visibility. Rather, their views have varied greatly, with no firm basis. The matter rests only on customary experience, which has no fixed mathematical rule. Some set the measure below ten degrees, while others set it higher. Their conflicting views on increasing or decreasing it resemble those of people who have attempted to fix the number of transmitters required for mass transmission to produce certain knowledge of what is reported. Yet there is no fixed numerical threshold for this, since knowledge depends on factors beyond numbers, just as sighting does.

All of this applies if the crescent is understood as that which has appeared in the sky, and complete cloud cover is treated as creating uncertainty. But if the crescent is understood as that which people have sighted and perceived, which has become visible to them and whose appearance they have announced aloud, this difficulty disappears in every case. The disagreement over this is well known among scholars within the school of Imam Ahmad and others. The second view is that of al-Shāfiʿī and others. And Allah knows best.

---

## Page 3030

Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked:

Concerning the creation of the heavens and the earth and the arrangement of the two luminaries and the stars: are they fixed in the celestial spheres, which move with them? Or do they move while the sphere remains stationary? Or do both move? Are the celestial spheres the heavens themselves, or are they distinct from them? Are the stars confined to the lowest heaven? If the sun and moon are in some of the heavens, does their light illuminate all the heavens? Do they move from one heaven to another? Are the earths seven in number, or are there creatures between them, or are some above others? Do the edges of the heavens rest upon a mountain, or is the earth within heaven like an egg within its shell, with the sea beneath that and the wind beneath it? Is there a sea above the heavens, beneath the Throne?

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah. These questions require an extensive discussion that this sheet cannot accommodate. The person asking them needs knowledge of several disciplines to receive fully satisfactory answers, for they involve disagreements and lengthy discussions. Nevertheless, we shall offer him an account as circumstances permit.

As for his question, “Are the celestial spheres the heavens themselves, or are they distinct from them?” there are two well-known views on this. Those who identify the two, however, cite as evidence the words of the Most High:

“Have you not seen how

---

## Page 3031

Allah has created seven heavens, one above another,”

“and placed the moon within them as a light, and made the sun a lamp.”

They say: Allah thus states that the moon is within the heavens. He, Most High, also says:

“And He is the One who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each floating in an orbit.”

And He, Most High, says:

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. Each is floating in an orbit.”

In these two verses, He states that the moon is in a celestial sphere, just as He states that it is within the heavens. Furthermore, Allah has told us that we see the heavens, saying:

“He who created seven heavens, one above another. You will see no inconsistency in the creation of the Most Merciful. Look again: do you see any cracks? Then look twice more: your sight will return to you humbled and weary.”

He also says:

“Have they not looked at the heaven above them—how We built it and adorned it, leaving it without any rifts?”

These and similar scriptural texts indicate that heaven is visible. What is visible is the celestial sphere, which indicates that the two are one and the same.

As for his question whether the sun and moon are moved independently of the celestial sphere, or whether their motion results from the sphere’s motion, this too is disputed. Most people, however, hold that their motion results from the motion of the sphere. As for the words of the Most High,

“Each is floating in an orbit,”

this does not preclude the floating He describes from being dependent upon the motion of the sphere, as is the case with night and day: their alternation depends upon the motion of something other than themselves. His words,

“Each is floating in an orbit,”

encompass the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, as He makes clear in Sūrat al-Anbiyā’.

---

## Page 3032

and likewise in Sūrat Yā Sīn:

“And a sign for them is the night: We strip the daylight from it, and at once they are in darkness.

“And the sun runs toward its appointed resting place. That is the determination of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.

“And the moon—We have determined phases for it, until it returns like an old date-palm stalk.

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. Each is floating in an orbit.”

Thus, His words, “Each is floating in an orbit,” encompass what precedes: the night, the day and the sun, as He mentions in Sūrat al-Anbiyā’. If He has described night and day as floating, although this depends on the motion of something else, then the same applies to His description of the sun and moon as floating in dependence on the celestial sphere. There is evidence for this, but this is not the place to set it out in detail.

As for the stars, Allah has told us that they adorn the lowest heaven, as He, Most High, says:

“Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the beauty of the stars.”

And He says:

“And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps.”

Some of those who hold that the celestial spheres are distinct from the heavens said that “the lowest heaven” here refers to the eighth sphere, in which astronomers say the fixed stars are situated. They claimed that those are the higher heavens, whereas the celestial spheres are the lower heavens. This view, however, rests on a weak foundation. Moreover, what we observe is the stars.

He, Most High, says:

“So I swear by those that recede,

“that move and withdraw.”

Receding means being concealed, which occurs before they appear in the east. Withdrawing is their return from the direction of the west. Thus, those that were concealed before rising withdraw after setting; while visible, they move, travelling from east to west.

---

## Page 3033

The sun and moon are in the celestial sphere, as Allah, Most High, has told us; they do not move from one heaven to another. The heavens are not connected to the earth, whether at Mount Qāf or anywhere else. Rather, the celestial spheres are round, as Allah and His Messenger have told us and as Muslim scholars and others have stated. Abū al-Husayn ibn al-Munādī, Abū Muhammad ibn Hazm, Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī and others have reported the consensus of Muslims that the celestial spheres are round.

Regarding His words,

“Each is floating in an orbit,”

Ibn ‘Abbās said: “In a circular form, like the whorl of a spindle.” In Arabic, falak denotes something round. The expression tafallaka thady al-jāriya means that a young woman’s breast has become rounded.

Allah created seven earths, one above another, as established in the authentic hadith collections from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever wrongfully takes a handspan of land will, on the Day of Resurrection, be made to wear a collar of it from seven earths.”

Abū Bakr al-Anbārī reported consensus on this, by which he meant the consensus of the people of hadith and Sunnah. Beneath the Throne is a sea, as related in the hadiths and mentioned in Quranic exegesis. Allah has also told us that He created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water.

The Throne is above all created things. It is the roof of the Garden of Eden, which is the highest part of Paradise, as established in the two Sahih collections from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.”

---

## Page 3034

Water surrounds most of the earth, and air surrounds both the water and the earth. Allah, Most High, has spread out the earth for His creatures and anchored it with mountains so that it does not sway, just as a ship is steadied with heavy weights when the sea grows rough; otherwise, it would sway. Allah, Most High,

“holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them in place after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.”

Allah—glory be to Him—upholds all created things above and below through His power. Whatever inherent properties and forces have been placed within them exist through His power and will—glory be to Him.

---

## Page 3035

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

“Did Allah create the heavens and the earth before night and day, or not?”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. “Night and day,” as brought about by the sun, are dependent upon the heavens and the earth. He did not create this night and this day before these heavens and the earth; rather, He created them as adjuncts to these heavens and the earth. When Allah causes the sun to rise, day comes, and when it sets, night comes. Day results from its appearance, and night from its setting. How, then, could this night and this day have existed before the sun, when the sun and the moon were created together with the heavens and the earth?

Allah, Most High, says:

“And it is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon—each floating in an orbit.”

And He, Most High, says:

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor can the night outstrip the day. Each floats in an orbit.”

Ibn ʿAbbās and others among the early generations said: “In a circle like the whorl of a spindle.”

Allah, Most High, has thus stated that night and day, the sun and the moon, are in the orbit. According to most scholars, “the orbit” means the heavens. The evidence is that Allah states in these two verses that the sun and the moon are in the orbit, while elsewhere He says:

“Have you not seen how Allah created

---

## Page 3036

seven heavens, one above another?”

“And placed the moon among them as a light, and made the sun a lamp.”

He thus states that He placed the sun and the moon in the heavens. Allah, Most High, also says:

“All praise is for Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light. Yet those who disbelieve set up equals to their Lord.”

He explains that He created the heavens and the earth, and that He created darkness and light, for “making” means causing something to become so. One says, “He made such-and-such,” meaning that he caused it to become so. He therefore mentions that He created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light, because darkness and light are brought about through the sun and the moon, which were created in the heavens. Darkness and light, night and day, are not independently existing bodies, but attributes and accidents subsisting in something else.

“Light” is the sun’s radiance and illumination, which Allah spreads through the air and over the earth. As for “the darkness of night,” some have said that it is likewise, while others have said that it is something with positive existence. Thus, this night and this day that alternate over us—one of which Allah causes to enter into the other, making night enter into day and day enter into night—succeed one another in turn. As Allah, Most High, says:

“Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of understanding.”

And He, Most High, says:

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor can the night outstrip the day.”

He, glorified be He, explains that He has assigned each thing a single measure that it does not exceed. The sun is not to overtake the moon and catch up with it. Rather, it has a course that Allah has ordained for it, and the moon has a course that Allah has ordained for it. As Allah, Most High, says:

“And a sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it, and behold, they are

---

## Page 3037

in darkness.”

“And the sun runs towards its resting place. That is the determination of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.”

“And the moon—We have ordained phases for it until it returns like an old date stalk.”

Then He says:

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor can the night outstrip the day.”

That is, it does not leave it behind and advance ahead of it so that a gap forms between them. Rather, they are joined together, neither separating from the other.

“Each floats in an orbit.”

The point is that Allah made this night and this day dependent upon these heavens and this earth. But before Allah created these heavens, this earth and this day, the Throne was upon water, as He, Most High, says:

“It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon water.”

Allah created these heavens from the vapour of that water. This is the smoke mentioned in His words, Most High:

“Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, ‘Come, willingly or unwillingly.’ They both said, ‘We come willingly.’”

“Then He formed them into seven heavens in two days.”

This was when water covered the earth’s soil and the wind blew over that water. Allah created these heavens and this earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. Those, then, are the days in which Allah, Most High, created these.

---

## Page 3038

He was asked—may Allah be pleased with him—about “the variation of night and day,” and the statement that it may be noon in Damascus while night has already fallen in another land: is this statement correct or not?

He replied—may Allah have mercy on him:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all worlds. Sunrise, the sun’s passage beyond the zenith, and sunset occur in the east before they occur in the west. Thus, the sun rises, passes beyond the zenith, and sets over India, China, and al-Khatt before it does so over the western lands. These events occur in Iraq before they occur in Greater Syria, and in Greater Syria before they occur in Egypt. The people of each locality are subject to the rulings determined by their own sunrise, the sun’s passage beyond the zenith, and sunset.

When dawn breaks in a locality, the time for the dawn prayer begins, and prayer and fasting become obligatory for its people, even if dawn has not yet broken elsewhere. The difference is slight between places close to one another. Between those in the farthest east and those in the farthest west, however, the difference is considerable—about half a full day. Allah, Glorified is He, has stated that the sun, the moon, the night, and the day all float

---

## Page 3039

in an orbit. Allah Most High says:

“It is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each floating in an orbit.”

And He says:

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. Each floats in an orbit.”

An “orbit” is circular, as stated by those Companions, Successors, and other Muslim scholars who discussed it. A circular object comes into view gradually, so those near it see it before those farther away. And Allah knows best.
